name: Lasombra Clan Disciplines: Flavor and Special Effects (Lasombra)

pages.name: Dominate, Potence, and Obtenebration Through Lasombra Eyes

text.content:
While Obtenebration shows the distinctive @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} nature most clearly, the clan's scholars believe that Dominate and Potence also reflect particular aspects of Lasombra's legacy. This page is flavor and interpretation guidance for Storytellers and players portraying Lasombra characters; it does not change the mechanics of the base Dominate, Potence, or Obtenebration powers already in the compendium.

Dominate

The Lasombra vampire doesn't just force her will on her target in a generic or abstract sense — she incises out part of the target's own will, leaving traces of herself inside his mind to direct him. A famous painting depicts a commanding Lasombra surrounded by two concentric circles of mortals: an inner circle whose eyes mirror his glory, and an outer circle whose shadows each contain a pitch-black silhouette of the vampire. That is how many Lasombra think of Dominate.

Potence

The clan abhors weaklings, but few Lasombra develop great strength in a purely physical sense — their supernatural vitality reflects the transformation of the vampire's body into something increasingly inhuman, rather than undead muscle and bone. For Christian Lasombra, mastery of Potence is a form of transubstantiation. Most Lasombra associate Potence with Obtenebration, treating it as the clan's shadow legacy reinforcing the vampire's own body rather than manifesting in the environment.

Obtenebration

Lasombra have spilled more blood and ink over Obtenebration's precise nature than over any other topic. The darkness Obtenebration calls forth has substance: it can entangle targets and inflict damage, and it absorbs sound and scent as well as light, yet it has no detectable chemical signature and no real weight. Depending on the Lasombra's inclinations, she may refer to the space where Obtenebration's shadow-stuff resides when not summoned as "outside," "beneath," or "beyond" the world. The prevailing answer to what the shadow-stuff actually is: "It's what it is. It's what you get when you do the thing that draws it out."

Storytellers should consider how the power strikes mortals nearby — it is disturbing on a very deep level, confronting people with proof that the world is very unlike what they thought, provoking both panic and moral revulsion (the same conviction that drives Inquisitors and hunters). Repeated, informed use of terrifying Obtenebration powers is a good way to erode a vampire's own Humanity in play.

The powers below already exist as mechanical Items in the disciplines compendium (Shadow Play, Shroud of Night, Arms of the Abyss, Black Metamorphosis, Tenebrous Form). This page adds @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}-specific flavor and optional detail from Clanbook: Lasombra without altering their existing mechanics.

Shadow Play

Many Lasombra find this one-dot power quite sufficient for most purposes. It doesn't just make shadows slide around for dramatic lighting — pieces of darkness come alive to wrap around victims, and animated shadows flying through the air don't yield to logical explanation the way enhanced Stealth or Intimidation might to a skeptical mortal witness.

Shroud of Night

Unlike Shadow Play's animated existing shadows, Shroud of Night brings forth something with no antecedent. The ball of tangible darkness is obvious to anyone outside it, though it can only remain a secret in an already-dark environment. Lasombra suffering Rötschreck often subconsciously invoke this power to hide from a perceived threat.

Arms of the Abyss

Shadow extrusions come to life and act without active concentration from their creator once evoked. Even the weakest tentacles are stronger and faster than the average mortal. Arms serve noncombat functions too: carrying a crippled vampire, passing through thin openings, or lying flat over a surface until needed.

Optional Rule — Sensory Feedback: spend one additional Blood Trait per tentacle to gain faint sensory impressions (touch, taste, pressure, temperature — not sight, sound, or smell) through that arm.

Lasombra in frenzy often subconsciously create Arms of the Abyss to help defeat whatever offends them.

Black Metamorphosis

No two Lasombra, not even sire and childe, look quite the same while undergoing this transformation — religious-iconography style, gods-of-darkness rigid/stylized style, or Lovecraftian non-Euclidean style, depending on the vampire's self-conception. The metamorphosed vampire doesn't look like a "vampire" to onlookers, making it a good psychological weapon and useful for impersonating demons to would-be occultists.

Optional Rule: any mortal previously victimized by this vampire's advanced Dominate (Conditioning or Possession) suffers a -1 Trait penalty on Courage checks when confronted with her Black Metamorphosis. If this reduces the victim's Courage to zero, it causes automatic panic plus partial amnesia.

Tenebrous Form

This power marks the threshold between control of shadow and identification with it — the Lasombra ceases being human even in form, becoming a disembodied will. Some Lasombra arrange a steady flow of victims to remain in this form as much as possible. A vampire in Tenebrous Form cannot fly, but can swim and suffers no harm from pressure; no confinement can hold it as long as an opening a few molecules wide exists.

Optional Rule: the Courage-penalty rule for Black Metamorphosis above may also apply to Tenebrous Form, at Storyteller discretion.

Wherever an Obtenebration power calls for spending Blood Traits, the blood pours out of a self-inflicted cut (or the vampire's mouth, tear ducts, etc.) and crawls to the area of effect. These self-inflicted cuts do not inflict any actual health-level damage, unless the vampire chooses otherwise for dramatic effect.

Powers that do not require spending Blood Traits instead draw shadows ejected from the vampire's mouth, self-inflicted cuts, or the folds of shadowed clothing, and the shadows retract the same way when the effect ends.

Evidence and residue: a failed or single-success Obtenebration attempt leaves a testable blood residue behind — a character with Enhanced Senses or similar investigative capability could identify the vampire responsible from it. Two or more successes let the vampire choose whether or not to leave any residue.

MET: spend one extra Trait of the relevant type (Physical, Social, or Mental, as fits the power) to gain the option of leaving a residue or not, at the player's discretion, regardless of how many successes/margin the challenge was won by.
